language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello! I am Ben, I'm an explorer and I live in Antarctica. Antarctica lies on the South Pole and it's always filled with ice and snow.
I am here to learn about the different aspects of the weather. I also want to look at the influence of the sun, wind, air pressure and humidity on weather.

Did you know that 70% of the earth's surface is covered with water, 27% with land and 3% with ice? The earth is moving around the sun and as a result of this there are different seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
How warm or cold these seasons are, is influenced by the weather. There are different types of weather such as sunny, rainy, windy and humid weather.
Here in Antarctica, there are a lot of penguins. I became friends with one of them. His name is Cosy. Can you help us learn the different aspects of the weather?
Hi, I am Tim. I'm here to help Ben and Cosy. Join me!

We look at the sun rising every day. Our sun gives us light, heat and energy. Without the sun it would be so cold that no living thing would be able to survive. Our planet would be completely frozen.

The sun defines the seasons, the harvests, and even the sleep patterns of all living creatures on earth. It may seem that energy comes from other sources such as gasoline and electricity, but the ultimate source of all energy is the sun.

Did you know that air has weight? We don't notice it, but it does. The weight of the air on the ground is called
"air pressure".
When the air above us is heavy, we call it high air pressure. When the air is light, we speak of low air pressure.
The weather plays a big role in influencing air pressure. High and low air pressure are caused because places on earth are not equally warmed by the sun.

For example, you can have a High Pressure System. A High Pressure System is a whirling mass of cool, dry air that generally brings fair weather and light winds. These bring
sunny skies.
There also exists a Low Pressure System. A Low Pressure System is a whirling mass of warm, moist air that generally brings stormy weather with strong winds.
So let's see if you can help me point out if the questions about Air Pressure are true or false.

Cosy would now like to learn about the wind.

Wind is air in motion. It is produced by the uneven heating of the earth's surface by the sun. Warm air, which weighs less than cold air, rises. Then cool air moves in and replaces the rising warm air. This movement of air is what makes the wind.
So let's see if you can help Cosy answer these questions about wind correctly.

Have you heard about humidity? Humidity describes the amount of water vapor in the air: the more water vapor present in air, the more humid it is. For example, rain is 100% humidity. Fog is less than 100% humidity. But both rain and fog are humid weather types.
As you can see in the picture, it is more humid when the temperature is low than when it is hot.
